articleTitle: An Efficient Approach for Short-Term Load Forecasting Using the Regression Learner Application
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: The regression method of forecasting allows businesses to use specific strategies so that those predictions, such as future sales, future needs for labor or supplies, or even future challenges, will yield meaningful information. In this paper, the use of the regression learner method for short-term load forecasting is performed. Its capabilities, advantages, and limitations are investigated using real load and weather data from the Hydro-Quebec database. Changes in electricity supply and demand have made their adjustment more complex. Our approach will be based on a predictive optimization method adapted to energy systems. This method is applied for the region of Mascouche (in Quebec, Canada) where the load varies between 60 megawatts and 140 megawatts.

articleTitle: Enhanced Power Optimization of Photovoltaic System in a Grid-Connected AC Microgrid Under Variable Atmospheric Conditions Using PSO-MPPT Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: The utilization of photovoltaic systems for generating clean electrical energy has witnessed a significant surge. Nevertheless, owing to their comparatively lower efficiency, scientists and experts have actively explored various strategies to enhance their efficacy and optimize their overall performance. This work introduces an enhanced approach for maximum power point tracking (MPPT) in grid-connected AC microgrids by employing a Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) controller. Using Matlab/Simulink, simulations were performed to create models of different system components, enabling a comparison of the performance between the two controllers under investigation: PSO and conventional P&O (Perturb and Observe). The findings clearly indicate that the implementation of the PSO algorithm for tuning MPPT control exhibits a more pronounced positive impact on optimizing power extraction when compared to the other strategies examined in this study.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Power Sharing Mechanism of a PEM Fuel Cell-Battery Powered Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: Evaluation of power sharing mechanism of a fuel cell-battery powered electric vehicle has been carried out using MATLAB and Simulink based mathematical simulation model. The vehicle simulation model was designed based on the specifications of a real-world commercial passenger vehicle to determine accurate estimation of onboard vehicle behaviors and power requirements depending on drive cycle inputs and vehicle dynamics. The power sharing mechanism is designed based on the role each component should be played by the vehicle's onboard hybrid combination of fuel cell and battery power sources. The battery is responsible for the meeting the vehicle's peak power demands whereas the fuel cell system controls the state-of-charge of the battery. The parameters of the power sharing mechanism are optimized by considering the drive torque, the battery state-of-the charge and the vehicle performance. The optimized simulation results showed that the power requirement/demand of the vehicle was significantly affected by the operating behaviors of the end users (driver) and combination of fuel cell and battery power sharing management system.

articleTitle: Development of Continuously Produced Thin-Walled Graphite-Polymer Bipolar Plates for Fuel Cells
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: Within the research project “InduRex”, thin-walled graphite-polymer bipolar plates for fuel cells are to be developed. The focus is on highly filled compound materials and process technologies for the continuous production of thin-walled foils. The entire process chain will be considered, starting with the selection of the raw materials used, through foil production to the insertion of the required structures. The physical and chemical target values defined by the “Department of Energy” are also set as targets for the foils. The focus of the scientific work is on a fundamental understanding of the material composition and its relationship to the final properties of the patterned bipolar plates, as well as their performance in a fuel cell stack. The fabricated bipolar plate foils were extensively characterized in terms of electrical resistances, H2 permeation, and others prior to a cell test to evaluate the impact of the production process on their quality. Furthermore in the research project “Faserverstärkte-Folien” carbon fibers are added to the foils to improve the mechanical properties. In addition to continuous production, the thin-walled foils were reinforced with carbon fibers using a hot press. The fiber-reinforced foils will be characterized in the next steps to investigate the influence of the carbon fibers. The aim is to obtain even thinner bipolar plates with consistent properties from the extruded foils in order to reduce the overall weight and volume of the fuel cell stack. This results in new challenges in the development of the bipolar plate design and the fuel cell stack.

articleTitle: Analysis of Brake Characteristics of Light-Duty Vehicles in Typical City in China
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: In November 2022, the European Union released the draft of the seventh stage emission regulations of light-duty vehicle. For the first time, non-exhaust emissions from light-duty vehicles were included in the regulation. In order to more accurately measure brake particle emissions, the European Union developed WLTC-Brake cycle based on the WLTC database for brake particle emissions measurement. This cycle unified the test conditions and avoided differences in test results caused by the lack of unified test cycle. In order to verify whether WL TC-Brake cycle is suitable for China's real roads, this paper collected real road driving data of 100 pure electric passenger cars in ten typical cities in China and analyzed the brake characteristics of the collected data. Results shown that China's real road brake characteristics are lower than those of WL TC-Brake cycle in terms of initial brake speed, average brake deceleration, brake duration, and brake interval. Therefore, it is necessary to develop a brake cycle that conforms to China's real road conditions to evaluate China's real road brake particle emission levels.

articleTitle: Review on Coral Reef Regeneration Methods through Renewable Powered Electrotherapy
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: The restoration of coral reef population in coastal regions is currently a growing concern. Many attempts have been made to apply new approaches to limit the deterioration of coral reefs, and to accelerate the growth of new reefs to protect coastal areas and ecosystems using available renewable energy sources. This paper highlights the new approaches and their various advantages and limitations in tidal and wave energy. The paper also suggests improvements to some of those systems using the recent developments in soft robotics, especially the use of biomimetic fish as a feasible support platform for the monitoring and maintenance of the power generation and potential restoration systems.

articleTitle: Mitigation of Cyber-Threat on Dynamic State Estimation
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: Dynamic state estimation plays a significant role in raising the situational awareness of cyber-physical energy systems. Determining the dynamic states of the system is dependent on the type of measurement data of the power grid and the tools used for the estimation such as Kalman filters (KF). However, due to the modernization of the power grid and the various tools for data acquisition, the grid has become vulnerable to new types of threats such as false data injections (FDIs) attacks. In this work, a new approach is presented to mitigate the impact of FDIs on dynamic state estimation. We use an unscented Kalman filter aided by eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGB) classifier as a two-stage approach to mitigate the impact of FDIs and cyber-threats. The proposed approach is tested on the New England IEEE 39-Bus System under different operating conditions. The results show the effectiveness of the proposed approach in mitigating the impact of UK-XGB on dynamic state estimation.

articleTitle: Analysis of Road Slope Characteristics in Chongqing City Based on Actual Vehicle Driving Data
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: This study aims to analyze the road gradient characteristics in Chongqing, China, with the intention of providing a reference basis for transportation planning, vehicle performance optimization, and sustainable urban development in the city. By utilizing data collected from the Chinese driving conditions data acquisition terminal and processing the collected vehicle driving data, we successfully established a road gradient characteristic database. The analysis results reveal that the average uphill proportion is 54.09%, with an average gradient of 2.98%; while the average downhill proportion is 42.85%, with an average gradient of -2.56%. Most road gradient variations are distributed between -8.7% and 10.48%, indicating a significant change in Chongqing's road gradients, particularly in uphill sections. The gradient change rate is primarily distributed between -0.2 and 0.2%/m. This study offers valuable insights for policymakers, automobile manufacturers, and urban planners in Chongqing and other similar mountainous cities.

articleTitle: Analysis of Emissions Characteristics and Fuel Consumption of Light-Duty Passenger Vehicles under Different Driving Cycles
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: China is about to fully implement the national VI-B standard. In the revision of the next stage emission standard for light vehicles, it is expected to add the China Light Vehicle Test Cycle (CLTC) on the basis of the existing World Light Vehicle Test Cycle (WLTC) certification, in order to achieve the requirements of coordinated development of energy consumption and emission standards, and conduct cold-start tests for automobiles. Based on this, three fuel vehicles were selected, and during the first-phase test, data such as THC, CO, NOx and particulate matter (PN) emissions, as well as fuel consumption data, were collected in real-time. According to the real-time emission data, the key factors affecting emissions under both WLTC and CLTC were analyzed. On the aspect of fuel consumption, a quantitative analysis and evaluation were conducted on idle, acceleration, deceleration, and constant speed conditions based on different cycle characteristics. The impact of out-of-cycle technologies, such as idle-stop and brake energy recovery systems, on energy consumption was also explained.

articleTitle: A Short-Term Prediction Model for Multi-energy Load of IES Based on Comprehensive Meteorological Index and Deep Learning Multi-network Fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: To improve community load situational awareness, cope with the stochastic and coupled nature of multiple energy load demands, and improve the accuracy of multi-energy load prediction, this paper proposes a short-term prediction model of multi-energy load for an integrated energy system based on comprehensive meteorological indices and deep learning multi-network fusion. Firstly, the basic construction of the integrated energy system is described. Secondly, a comprehensive meteorological index based on biometeorological indicators is introduced and the ReliefF feature selection algorithm is used to construct a correlation model between the meteorological index and loads. Then, a convolutional neural network and Bi-directional long short-term memory load prediction model that introduces the attention mechanism is developed by applying a deep learning multi-network fusion approach. Finally, the scientific and feasibility of the model is verified through the analysis of a case study. The results show that the model proposed in this paper can effectively improve the accuracy of integrated energy system load forecasting.

articleTitle: Renewable Energy Experiment and Teaching Innovation: Experimental Teaching Mode of Solar Cell Manufacturing Process Based on PV Factory
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: The development of renewable energy can not be separated from the teaching innovation of experimental courses of energy specialty. The preparation technology of large solar energy batteries is a required course for students majoring in new energy, which has the characteristics of experiment and application. However, the shortage of experimental resources and experimental funds make it impossible for many students to start the experiment. In order to solve this problem, based on the PV Factory simulation software, this paper simulates the production process of the aluminum backfield p-type battery sheet in industry, and innovatively designs the experimental teaching mode of solar cell preparation. In the experimental teaching mode of this paper, the students simulate the preparation steps of solar cells through the PV Factory simulation software. In practice, the PV Factory simulation software will refine the solar cell preparation process to 12 small steps, 28 physical and chemical reactions, and 24 process parameters. Students can design and generate solar cells by adjusting the parameters of each response. On the one hand, it is the first time to use software to simulate the preparation of solar cells and use it in the experimental courses of College students, which creatively solves the problems of shortage of experimental resources and insufficient learning time. On the other hand, the experimental method creatively restores the whole process of solar cell preparation, resolves the problem that theoretical knowledge learning and experimental operation are not synchronized in the experimental teaching, and promotes students' deep understanding of the whole process of solar cell preparation. The experimental teaching mode designed in this paper can also train students' good scientific literacy through a variety of parameter settings, rigorous experimental simulation process, exercise their problem solving ability.

articleTitle: Increasing Biodiesel Production Using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: Microalgae are an excellent source of biomass for next generation biodiesel production. In this study, both theoretical and experimental tests of variables such as lipase, methanol, algal oil concentration, incubation time and temperature used in biodiesel production were performed using RSM, ANN and IRS modeling. According to results, the highest experimental and theoretical biodiesel efficiencies were 87%, 87.5% at 1 % lipase, 2 ml of methanol, 0.2 g of algal oil, 6 h of incubation time and 45 °C of temperature, respectively. Also, we modelled the variables via interactive response surface (IRS). Maximum biodiesel efficiencies of full quadratic and interaction models were 80.1504% and 75.4416% at 1.7917% of lipase, 1.1722 mL of methanol, 0.575 g of algal oil, 4.0833 h of incubation time and 40.2778 °C of temperature, respectively. In conclusion, Biodiesel yield can be increased by changing parameters such as lipase, methanol, algal oil, incubation time and temperature.

articleTitle: Travel Scenario Characteristics Effects on the Energy Consumption Deterioration of Electric Vehicles under Low Temperature
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: The deterioration of energy consumption under low temperature is a key issue that hinders the development of pure electric vehicles (PEVs) in cold regions, which travel scenario characteristics is one of the factors leading to the deterioration. This study compared travel characteristics of the actual road driving data in the commuting scenario and the operation scenario, then conducted the energy consumption testing in environmental simulating test chamber at -20°C through two methods which can faithfully reflect the scenario travel characteristics, Segmentation Cycle Method and Consecutive Cycle Method. The test results show that the energy consumption of the two scenarios at -20 °C decreases by 193% and 152% respectively compared with that at room temperature, 23°C, and the energy consumption of the commuting scenario is about 16.7% higher than that of the operation scenario. Long parking duration is the main manifestation of the travel characteristics of the commuting scenario. The primary reason of energy consumption deterioration is the repeated heating of the air conditioner, accounting for 10.2%. The research shows that the applicable test method is an important factor for accurate energy consumption, and the Segmentation Cycle Method proposed this study can provide effective reference for product performance evaluation.

articleTitle: Influence of Annealing Temperature on the Nanostructural Formation of Ti4Ti5O12 Lithium Battery Anode Material
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: In this study, Li<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>Ti<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf> (LTO) was synthesized by the sol-gel method, and the influence of the annealing temperature on the formation of the spinel structure of the material was studied for its use as anode material in lithium batteries. The structures of the synthesized materials were evaluated by X-ray diffraction (XRD), while the morphology, by scanning electron spectroscopy (SEM). LTO nanocrystals with a particle size between 24 and 35 nm joined in highly porous agglomerates were obtained. LTO nanocrystals with TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> impurities in their anatase and rutile phases were obtained at temperatures below 700 °C, diffusing from this temperature and obtaining higher purity LTO nanocrystals in the spinel phase at temperatures above 750 °C. The lattice parameter calculations confirm the successful formation of the material.

articleTitle: The Energy Supply of Water Desalination Units Using Renewable Energies
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: There is an increasing requirement to supply clean energy to satisfy water desalination energy demands. However, there are opportunities to improve the financial feasibility of green energy production. This paper investigates the energy supply of water desalination units using renewable energies, aiming to decrease the cost of the system operation. This will be achieved primarily by improved energy scheduling and management methods. The proposed optimal energy management strategy will allow for increased flexibility in how energy is supplied to the water desalination units, as well as when it produces the most revenue. The proposed method is applied on a case study to extract the simulation results and discussion. This method directly contributes to providing additional clean power to the grid, which will be the basis to determine how large the potential of this offset can be.

articleTitle: Low Carbon Cities, Green Mobility as a Mechanism for the Development of Sustainable Cities & Environmental Sustainability. The Case of the Valparaíso Trolley as a Green Means of Transport, Chile
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: The main objective of this work is to explore whether, in the future in which new high-investment electric transport is implemented, trolleys as a means of transport can be a consolidation mechanism such as a sustainable city together with environmental sustainability. The case of the Valparaíso trolleys is selected, since (1) they are a green means of transportation, (2) they move exclusively with electricity, since the beginning of the 20th century (3) they reduce the pollution of the place, (4) they favor uses transportation alternatives, (5) they are axes of social encounter of the community, (5) given their industrial heritage, they are a tourist-cultural resource in the area. The methodology is carried out through the analysis of pollution and energy savings of the trolleys throughout the time they have been operational. In this way you can measure the environmental impact they generate and how sustainable it is to continue using them as a means of transportation in the city. It is concluded that facilitating the daily use of trolleys turns out to be a consolidation mechanism as a sustainable city together with environmental sustainability, as observed in Valparaíso and the various routes of these machines.

articleTitle: Modeling and Analysis of a Thermoelectric Power Generator
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: Thermoelectric Generator (TEG) was developed using the Seebeck phenomenon. It consists of many thermocouples connected thermally in parallel and electrically in series to increase energy efficiency. TEGs instantly convert thermal energy to electrical energy with no rotating parts and are less likely to fail due to no moving parts. With the rising cost of fossil fuels and their negative impact on the atmosphere, it is time to consider TEGs as renewable energy sources with applications ranging from mW to W power. This study derives a mathematical model of a TEG module and validates it with MATLAB/SIMULINK.

articleTitle: Numerical Study on the Catalytic Combustion Characteristics of Ultra-Low Calorific Value Coalbed Methane
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: The ultra-low calorific value coalbed methane is of great significance to the safe production of coal mines. However, due to its low methane concentration, it is generally emitted directly into the atmosphere, which not only causes environmental pollution, but also energy waste. Presently, catalytic combustion has become the most promising methods for the conversion and utilization of ultra-low calorific value coalbed methane with its high efficiency and green characteristics. Based on the field investigation of ultra-low calorific value coalbed methane emission in a typical mine of an energy company in Panzhou City, this paper uses the method of computational fluid dynamics to simulate the catalytic combustion characteristics of ultra-low calorific value coalbed methane. Result shows that the catalyst has a positive effect on the catalytic combustion of ultra-low calorific value coalbed methane, under the conditions of this paper, the lower the flow rate, the more significant the catalytic effect. Increasing the inlet temperature can improve the catalytic reaction efficiency.

articleTitle: Impact of Reservoir Evaporation on Determining Power Purchasing Agreement under Solar-Hydro Hybridization
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: Installing floating solar photovoltaics (FPV) on reservoirs is a relatively new but rapidly emerging technology in the renewable energy sector. The combination of solar and hydro can produce fully dispatch able renewable electricity and facilitate the integration of FPV onto the grid. The benefits of solar-hydro hybridization are especially noticeable in areas with pronounced dry and wet seasons. In those areas, the evaporation loss from the reservoir cannot be ignored. This paper presents how evaporation is mathematically included in an operational hydro scheduling tool. The proposed modeling method updates evaporation loss based on the dynamic changes of the reservoir surface area. The numerical results show that less availability of water resources caused by evaporation will lead to a 7.5% reduction in maximum firm load obligation. Evaporation in solar-hydro hybridization is a vital factor that cannot be ignored when determining a reliable power purchasing agreement.

articleTitle: Enhancing Frequency Deviation of a Microgrid in Connected Mode Using Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: The demand for electric power has been increasing salient lately, causing carbon emissions from energy goes up by more than half when compared to the period when the industrial revolution began, that raising concerns about global warming. As a result, the researchers focused on the movement toward renewable energy, including solar energy, wind energy, and biomass energy, rather than conventional energy, which depends on fuel. Because the generation point of electric power is relatively far from the point of consumption, therefore electric power transmission lines are the means of delivering energy to the consumer, it has become important to study the electrical system and develop the most appropriate solutions to the problems that occur in it. One of the researchers' top priorities is keeping the system's frequency stable. Various smart solutions were utilized in the researchers' studies to adjust the frequency stability of power systems. An artificial intelligence-based technique was utilized for modeling the proper control of the frequency of the microgrid, like the operation of the human brain. In this study, a model of a microgrid with a solar-energy station connected to the main grid was designed. The control that will use the PSO algorithm to enhance PID was compared and analyzed, and the smart controllers were designed and tested using MATLAB.

Author Keywords: ITAE (Integral of Time multiplied by Absolute Error)

articleTitle: Research on Drilling and Backfilling Treatment of Ground Source Heat Pump in Buried Pipe
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: Low-cost, efficient use of drilling pulp, on-site drilling treatment backfill, can realize the reuse of construction waste, reduce the harm of drilling to the environment. Based on the original pulp backfill materials at the engineering site, different proportions of cement, water reducing agent, expansion agent, natural graphite powder and other materials were added for treatment and experiment, and performance parameters such as thermal conductivity, porosity, fluidity, compressive strength, shrinkage rate and other performance parameters were selected for the physical property optimization analysis of the backfill material. The results show that the optimal mass ratio scheme of drilling and backfill material additives is: mortar ratio 0.6, liquid-solid ratio 0.3, water reducing agent and expansion agent addition amount of 2 % and 6% of cement mass, and graphite addition amount is 1 % of the total solid mass. In order to ensure that the backfill material densely fills the cavity between the U-shaped pipe and the drilled hole and facilitates on-site backfilling construction, the flow degree of the backfill should not be less than 185mm.

Author Keywords: buried pipe ground source heat pump system

articleTitle: A Review on Sustainable Application of Tyre Derived Activated Carbon in Energy Storage Device
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: Tyre is a common form of non-degradable polymer-based solid waste. As it is abundant in quantity and takes a long time to decompose, it is complicated to manage this waste. This solid waste can be effectively managed by converting it into char through the pyrolysis process, and then converting char into activated carbon (AC) through physical and chemical activation processes. Tyre-derived activated carbon (TDAC) has multiple applications, such as absorber, catalyst, and electrode material, among others. This study reviews different production processes, and applications of TDAC. The abstracts of n= 197 papers were critically analysed for this review. Finally, n=11 full-length articles were selected through PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analysis) bibliographic search method for a thorough investigation of production processes, properties, relationship between activation process and properties, and applications of TDAC. Both physical and chemical activation processes can produce a large surface area and a microporous structure on TDAC. The study found that both processes can produce AC with a surface area ranging from 400 to 900 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/g. However, the chemical activation process with potassium hydroxides (KOH) is found preferable because it has the capability to increase surface area at less time and temperature. The focus of the study was evaluated the application of TDAC as electrode material. In several experimental studies, TDAC was utilised as an electrode in numerous energy storage devices, including supercapacitors, batteries, and fuel cells, as TDAC has high specific-capacitance properties.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review of Cyber Security Enhancements for PMU Communications in Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: Phasor Measurement Units (PMUs) are crucial components for monitoring the operational conditions of smart grids. As the PMU communication network often spans a wide area, it is susceptible to cyber-attacks. The current communication standard for PMU communication, IEEE C37.118.2, lacks explicit security measures to defend PMU data against cyber threats. The absence of robust security measures leaves the PMU communication network vulnerable to potential disruptions. A compromise in the integrity of transmitted PMU data can have severe consequences, such as grid outages. To address these challenges, this paper presents a comprehensive review of existing literature on cyber security enhancements for PMU communications. The review focuses on identifying vulnerabilities and potential threats to PMU systems and explores various techniques and strategies proposed to mitigate these risks. Topics covered include secure communication protocols, intrusion detection systems, encryption algorithms, authentication mechanisms, and anomaly detection techniques. By providing an overview of the current state of research, this review aims to highlight the importance of securing PMU communications and identify future directions for enhancing cyber security in this domain.

articleTitle: A Comparison of Status Update Optimization and Microgrid Management
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: Provision of timely power supply to digital networks through smart microgrids represents a relevant research challenge. In next generation communication systems, high power demands are caused by the need for an efficient management of real-time content and guaranteeing up-to-date context awareness to computationally heavy applications. Such an integrated communication-energy challenge is gaining momentum in the research community, but, possibly due to different timescales, the problems of energy provision and data networking are often investigated with different approaches and mindsets. In this paper, we argue that they both stem from a fundamentals problem of efficient resource management that can ultimately be treated via dynamic programming as a unifying analytical tool. To this end, we show how the problems of energy management in a smart microgrid can be tackled through a framework conceived for the optimization of age of information. This allows to infer useful conclusions and, at the same time, the similarity can be expanded to leverage existing analytical procedure and derive efficient approaches, especially concerning the insertion of distributed intelligence in the control mechanisms.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Feature Selection and Construction Method for Detection of Wind Turbine Generator Heating Faults
publicationTitle: 2023 4th International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: Data preprocessing is crucial to create effective machine learning applications. Feature construction and selection are powerful techniques used for this aim. In this paper, a feature selection and construction approach is presented for the detection of wind turbine generator heating faults. The data used for this study was obtained from the Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system of a wind turbine. The original features directly collected from the data collection system consist of wind characteristics, operational data, temperature measurements and status information. In addition to these original features, new features were created in the feature construction step to obtain information that can be more powerful indications of the faults. After the construction of new features, a hybrid feature selection technique was implemented to find out the most relevant features in the overall set to increase the classification accuracy and decrease the computational burden. Feature selection involves two parts which are filter-based and wrapper-based approaches. Filter based feature selection was applied to exclude the features which are non-discriminative and wrapper-based method was used to determine the final features considering the redundancies and mutual relations amongst them. Artificial Neural Networks were used both in the detection phase and as the induction algorithm of the wrapper-based feature selection part. The results show that, the proposed approach contributes to the fault detection system to be more reliable especially in terms of reducing the number of false fault alarms.
